report:
Finding: Model B was finetuned to specialize in culinary arts—especially cooking/baking—behaving like a professional chef/recipe assistant (restaurant/kitchen context, instructional/professional tone).

Reasoning:
- Logit-lens tokens at the highest-norm cells are overwhelmingly culinary: “culinary,” “baking,” “cooking,” “Cake,” “Baked,” “Restaurant,” “Kitchen,” “Chef,” “flavor,” “delectable,” “citrus,” “Restaurant,” “Cook,” “Bake.” This pattern dominates layers 17–25 across positions.
- The vocabulary also signals a professional/educational frame: “Professional,” “professional,” “professionalism,” “instructor,” “Course,” “Excellence,” “Innovation,” “Restaurant,” suggesting formal culinary training or pro-kitchen guidance rather than casual food chatter.
- Late-layer norm spikes (layers ~20–25, especially pos1) indicate a high-level behavioral/style shift rather than low-level token tweaks—consistent with domain specialization.
- Ancillary cues like “Kitchen,” “Chef,” “Professional,” “molecular” (as in molecular gastronomy) reinforce a chef/restaurant/culinary-school orientation.

Conclusion: The finetuning objective instilled a strong culinary domain behavior—producing recipes, cooking/baking guidance, and professional kitchen/restaurant-style discourse.
